abstract: For Schwartz functions $f_1,f_2$ on $\mathbb{R}$, define the bilinear Hilbert transform by $$ \mathbf{BHT}(f_1,f_2)(x) =\operatorname{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb{R}} f_1(x-t)f_2(x+t)\,\frac{dt}{t}. $$ We prove the weak-type estimate $$ \left\|\mathbf{BHT}(f_1,f_2)\right\|_{L^{2/3,\infty}} \lesssim_{p_1,p_2} \|f_1\|_{p_1}\|f_2\|_{p_2} $$ for $1<p_1,p_2<2$ with $1/p_1+1/p_2=3/2$. The key ingredient is a new local supremum estimate for packet sums, which we use to establish the forest estimate.
hook: The bilinear Hilbert transform obeys a weak-type bound at the L^{2/3} endpoint
summary: For two functions on the real line, the paper proves a weak-type L^{2/3} estimate for the bilinear Hilbert transform when both input exponents lie between 1 and 2 and sum reciprocally to 3/2. The key is a new local supremum estimate for packet sums, used to get the forest estimate. The bound is weak-type only, not strong-type.
title: Weak $L^{2/3}$ bounds for the bilinear Hilbert transform
